title: Benedict, again
hook: listen with the ear of your heart
tomorrow: why did a rich kid in Assisi hand back even his clothes?

segments.voice: Yesterday, Aquinas: grace perfects, finishing what God already called good. Today, a monk who started everything with one word.

Earbuds in, nodding along, thinking about what you'll say next: half-listening is a skill now. So here's the first word of the Rule of Benedict, the short book monks and nuns still live by. Not pray. Not obey. Not God. The first word is listen. In its own Latin, ausculta. Listen, my child, to the teaching of the master, and incline the ear of your heart. Where does a life with God begin? For Benedict, with your ears.
screen: `HALF-LISTENING IS A SKILL NOW.` → `THE FIRST WORD: AUSCULTA.` → `THE EAR OF YOUR HEART.`

segments.voice: The ear of your heart means listening that changes what you do, not just what you hear. Benedict borrows a psalm to say it, in the Douay-Rheims Bible: "To day if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts." Here's the one to tell a friend: in his Rule, Benedict tells the abbot to call the whole community together for big decisions, even the youngest, because the Lord often shows what is better to the younger one. Listening runs downhill and uphill. Now a neighbor who also begins with listening. The Torah, in Deuteronomy, gives Israel the words Jews call the Shema, in the 1917 Jewish translation: "Hear, O Israel: the LORD our God, the LORD is one." The same chapter asks for these words to be spoken "when thou liest down, and when thou risest up," and Jewish tradition, in the Mishnah, sets the Shema in the evening and the morning. Jesus quoted those same opening words when he was asked for the first commandment. So the shared ground is real: before you speak to God, hear. And the difference is honest. The Shema is Israel's own declaration of the one God, at the heart of the Jewish covenant, said at home and at bedtime. Benedict's listen opens a rule for monks living together under an abbot. Catholics confess the one God as Father, Son and Holy Spirit, which Jewish tradition doesn't. Two houses, each with its own door. Both doors open with the same first word.
screen: `HARDEN NOT YOUR HEARTS.` · `EVEN THE YOUNGEST GETS HEARD.` · `HEAR, O ISRAEL.` · `TWO HOUSES, ONE FIRST WORD.` · then, large: `LISTEN.`

segments.voice: Choose one sound near you: a fan, traffic, a bird, your own breathing. Listen to it fully, as if it were someone speaking to you, and when your mind wanders, come back to it. If you pray, you can begin with the psalm Benedict quotes: today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts.
Benedict. The monk whose Rule opens on one word, listen, with the ear of the heart.
Keep this: listen, the first word in Benedict's Rule and the first word of the Shema too. Good night.
